children: The narrative coming from senior officials at the Reserve Bank of Australia remains hawkish and bets on a further interest rate rise this month have increased. Still, the RBA are between a rock and a hard place with inflation too high while activity in the economy is clearly "starting to break" in areas such as the housing market and private credit lending, says Andrew Canobi, director of fixed income at Franklin Templeton Australia. An interest rate increase this month looks to be a close call, he adds. If the RBA decide to hike from here it gets increasingly bullish for short-end bonds as the economy will slow quickly led by the consumer, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; X @JamesGlynnWSJ)
